description.narrative: The project will rehabilitate about 1,200 kilometers (km) of rural roads in ten provinces (Banteay Meanchey, Battambang, Kampong Cham, Kampong Chhnang, Kampong Speu, Kampong Thom, Pursat, Siem Reap, Takeo and Thbuong Khmum) to paved condition. The rehabilitated roads will provide poor rural provinces with a safer, cost-effective rural road network with all-year access to markets and other social services. The project will also support a sustainable road maintenance regime in the Ministry of Rural Development (MRD), a community-based road safety program, an HIV/AIDS and human trafficking awareness and prevention program (HHTPP), and climate change adaptation measures.

Rural road safety and community awareness program Indicator: By 2022, 40% of residents (50% women) in project provinces and all contractors' personnel participate in an HHTPP before and during civil works construction. Achievement: 58 Progress/Status: Achieved. Residents: Implementation of the HHTPP was completed in January 2022. Cumulative achievements include a total of 415,245 residents, of which 240,518 were women (or 58%), individual community members including construction workers and members of the Commune and District AIDS Committees have been reached out against 410,090 of the 40% DMF target.
Other achievements as of end of January 2022: (i) 382,466 local residents including 226,018 women (59%) including: (ii) 8,854 construction workers including 1,081 women (12.2%) (iii) 360 members of commune and district AIDS committees including 180 women (50%); and 23,565 people were referred for blood-test and STI service including 13,239 women (56%) have been received the HHTPP awareness raising from the program.
Overall cumulative achievement as of January 2022 is 40.5% against the 40% of the DMF. COVID-19 pandemic was observed as one of key challenges for raising awareness to community. Data Source: Quarterly progress reportssss: MRD

Average travel times (minutes) per trip on project roads decreased to 30 minutes in 2023 Achievement: 39 Progress/Status: The end-line survey conducted in November 2022 have shown that the travel time spent by the respondents and their household members after the road has been improved was estimated at an average time (from house to nearby markets, health center/ hospitals located at the district road or at the end point of the improved road) at 21 minutes for both male and female, compared to more than 1 hour when the road was still laterite (source: Endline Survey for RRIP II and RRIP II-AF, December 2022, Table 40). Road crash rate in the project area per 1,000 beneficiaries decreased by 20% by 2023. Achievement: 20 Progress/Status: Community Base-road safety program was completed in May 2021. The completion report revealed the road crash rate per 1,000 beneficiaries along the project roads was 0.145 in 2020. The traffic crash rate, which continued to grow until 2019, then decreased by 10% in 2020. Hence, The the crash rate would be decreased over 20% by 2023. Data Source: National road safety action plan annual report: National Road Safety Committee
Field traffic surveys: MRD
